candidates.title: Unhashed config field hash_tree.phtc_size makes adoption and every later store/clone cost unbounded memory and disk, and is carried into the operator's own snapshots
candidates.component: Loading and storing machines (machine_config::load, hash_tree / page_hash_tree_cache constructor and clear, machine::store, machine::clone_stored)
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md: 'storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines'); also the PRT player and CLI (support) which reach it
candidates.location: src/hash-tree.cpp:979-1004 (hash_tree ctor passes config.phtc_size to page_hash_tree_cache unchecked); src/page-hash-tree-cache.hpp:412-454 (maps get_storage_length(num_entries), m_map.reserve(num_entries), placement-new of every payload), :461-473 (only bound is ptrdiff_t max), :597-605 (clear() writes every entry); src/machine.cpp:502-516 (store writes the full phtc data and m_c with phtc_size), :520-570 (clone_stored clones phtc and config.json verbatim); src/machine-config.cpp:125-151 (load takes phtc_size from config.json); src/json-util.cpp:1784
candidates.description: hash_tree.phtc_size (number of entries of the page hash-tree cache) is read from the stored config.json and is neither part of the hashed state nor of any valid-template condition, and nothing bounds it except ptrdiff_t overflow. The operator's machine allocates an unordered_map bucket array of phtc_size entries, maps a phtc file of ~12 KiB x phtc_size, and on load (fresh/uninitialized cache: placement-new of every payload) and on clear_hash_tree (page_hash_tree_cache::clear walks every entry) writes ~12 KiB per entry: into private memory with SHARING_NONE (CLI --load, jsonrpc spawn in prt.new_machine), into the shared clone file with SHARING_ALL (PRT player new_stored_player). The value is then copied into config.json of every snapshot the operator writes (machine::store writes m_c; clone_stored copies config.json byte for byte), and store() writes ~8 KiB x phtc_size of non-pristine pristine-page-trees into each snapshot's hash_tree.phtc. There is no documented way to change phtc_size of a loaded machine (CLI --load ignores --hash-tree; the hash_tree config is not a runtime option). A supplier ships a valid template whose phtc file is a sparse zero file (cheap to transfer) and phtc_size large; the honest operator's adoption under O1 exhausts memory (OOM kill) or disk (SIGBUS on a shared mapping of a sparse file when the disk fills), and every snapshot it then writes keeps the cost. A template created with the documented CLI option --hash-tree=phtc_size:N is itself a valid template, so no forgery is even needed.
candidates.trigger: Template supplier (any party that hands the operator the template directory, or the application developer who created it with --hash-tree=phtc_size:N). Operator follows O1: cartesi-machine --load=T --clear-hash-tree --store=..., or Lua cartesi.machine(T,{clear_hash_tree=true}), or the PRT player new_stored_player (clone_stored + load SHARING_ALL + clear_hash_tree).
candidates.reachability: The template meets every valid-template condition: its hashed contents and root hash are unchanged (rebuilt root 0x428a6bb8... in the experiment). phtc_size is not hashed and is a documented configuration option (cartesi-machine --hash-tree=phtc_size:<number>, manual hash_tree_config), so the machine was 'created from a configuration'. Nothing on the honest operator's path rewrites it.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The exclusion 'Defects triggered only by loading a snapshot that the emulator did not write and that does not meet the conditions of a valid template' does not apply: it meets them, and the same section says 'Once a snapshot meets them, nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory.' 'Defects that need the cached hash-tree data ... to survive its adoption without a rebuild (O1)' does not apply: the defect happens during and after the rebuild. 'Host faults, such as a full disk' does not apply: the disk/memory exhaustion is caused by the emulator's handling of an unhashed field, not a host fault. One reading could argue section 4 trusts 'the valid template it chose to defend'; but trust there is about contents, and R4 says 'Every reproducible configuration that the emulator accepts ... yields a machine on which this rule holds. A configuration that would not is rejected when the machine is created.'
2 Role: storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines and the hash tree are 'Honest operator' (AUDIT.md component table). The CLI and PRT player reach it too (support).

3 High/Medium cases: not a verifier, not an unreachable state. The High case 'A crash, hang, memory-safety defect or unbounded allocation in a component in the honest-operator role, caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline' fits if triage reads the template as data the operator may decline (it can refuse templates). The constant-factor High case does not fit: the cost is unbounded in phtc_size.

4 Critical: on the honest operator's path ('Obtaining its valid template ... rebuilding its cached hash-tree data (O1)'; 'Storing and reloading the machine'), it violates R12: 'storing, loading, cloning or syncing a machine' must have 'a worst case in host time and memory that is bounded and at most linear in ... the bytes it covers', and the Critical case 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost ... larger than what the deployment was sized for'; it also violates R4 ('Every reproducible configuration that the emulator accepts ... yields a machine on which this rule holds ... A configuration that would not is rejected when the machine is created') and the section 8 sentence 'nothing it carries outside the hashed state may ... crash the honest operator'.

5 Not needed. Deciding facts between High and Critical: whether a template the operator adopts counts as 'data from other parties that the honest operator may decline' (High) or as the valid template on its path (Critical).
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure: the honest operator cannot obtain/keep its template within the resources the deployment was sized for (OOM kill, disk full, SIGBUS), cannot store its per-input snapshots (each carries the cost), and cannot respond in time; if the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim wins.
candidates.evidence: Copied bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template/machine (phtc_size 4096, 33 MB). With phtc_size 4096: load+clear peak RSS 140 MB. Set phtc_size=65536 in config.json and replaced hash_tree.phtc with a sparse zero file of the required length (template on disk: 756 KB): same rebuilt root 0x428a6bb8...ac75, peak RSS 880 MB (SHARING_NONE and SHARING_ALL), machine:store of the adopted machine wrote a 517 MB snapshot (hash_tree.phtc 515 MB allocated, apparent 807 MB) whose config.json still has phtc_size 65536; clone_stored + load SHARING_ALL + clear grew the clone from 756 KB to 772 MB. Cost is linear in phtc_size (~12 KiB/entry), and phtc_size is bounded only by ptrdiff_t (e.g. 2^30 -> ~12 TiB mapping, 8 GiB m_map.reserve). Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERTEMPLATE/scripts/craft.py, load.lua. Also checked phtc_size=1: hashes, proofs and node hashes equal the default (no wrong hash).
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: copy the baremetal-template, set config.hash_tree.phtc_size to 2^20 and truncate hash_tree.phtc to the matching sparse length; in a child process with ulimit -v of ~2 GB, load with {clear_hash_tree=true}, check the root hash equals the on-chain/root-hash.txt, store it, and assert (a) the load succeeds within the limit and (b) the stored snapshot's config.json phtc_size and hash_tree.phtc size are independent of the template's value (e.g. at most the default, or bounded by the state size). Fails today (load OOMs/fails, or the snapshot inherits 2^20).

candidates.title: store_first_epoch_checkpoint takes the template hash from un-rebuilt cached hash-tree data, and crisium compares it with the on-chain template hash (O1 violated by the reference player)
candidates.component: PRT player recipes: doc/recipes/prt.lua store_first_epoch_checkpoint; doc/recipes/crisium.lua open_epochs; doc/recipes/prt-demo.lua
candidates.role: Support (PRT player, AUDIT.md table); stands in for the honest operator's template adoption
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua:2743-2777 (clone_stored(template), cartesi.machine(temporary_directory) without clear_hash_tree, template_hash = machine:get_root_hash() at :2763, written as initial_state_hash/final_state_hash of epoch.json); doc/recipes/prt.lua:3226-3241 load_epoch_checkpoint (initial_state_hash = manifest.final_state_hash); doc/recipes/crisium.lua:234-236 (assert(manifest.final_state_hash == on-chain getTemplateHash)); prt-demo.lua:76 and :131
candidates.description: The epoch-0 checkpoint is made by cloning the template directory and loading the clone without rebuilding its cached hash-tree data; the root hash read from that machine (the supplier's cached dht/dpt) becomes the checkpoint's final_state_hash. crisium then compares that cached hash with the on-chain template hash, and new_stored_player later rebuilds and asserts the rebuilt hash equals the cached one. The threat model says 'A root hash read from a machine loaded without that rebuild does not check this condition' and O1 requires the operator to rebuild 'and only then compare the root hash with the on-chain commitment'. With a valid template whose cache is stale or forged, the checkpoint records a wrong hash: crisium refuses the valid template ('epoch 0's checkpoint is not the template'), and since store_first_epoch_checkpoint returns early when the directory exists, rerunning never repairs it. Conversely an invalid template with a cache claiming the commitment passes crisium's check and is only caught by the later assertion in new_stored_player (crash loop under prt-supervise). The checkpoint also keeps the supplier's cached hash-tree files and config.json unchanged.
candidates.trigger: Template supplier ships a template whose hashed contents equal the on-chain commitment but whose .dht/.dpt cache describes other contents (e.g. built with one RAM byte different, then the byte restored). Operator runs prt-demo / crisium which call store_first_epoch_checkpoint.
candidates.reachability: Valid template, only cached hash-tree data crafted (explicitly allowed in the persona; the threat model says loading does not check it). Reproduced.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? 'Defects that need the cached hash-tree data of a stored machine the operator did not produce to survive its adoption without a rebuild (O1)' excludes defects that need the operator to skip the rebuild; here the reference implementation itself skips it, and section 5 says 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too. The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them'. Not excluded.
2 Role: the PRT player and crisium are Support ('No production deployment runs the player'). 'A defect that only a support component shows is never above Medium.'

3 Medium case: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. In the operator role, refusing its valid template (cannot defend) is a completeness failure on the honest operator's path ('Obtaining its valid template ... rebuilding its cached hash-tree data (O1)'), which would be Critical.
4 n/a (capped at Medium by step 2/3).
5 n/a.
candidates.threat_to_goal: In a node built on this reference, the honest operator either refuses the valid template it must defend (never plays epoch 0, so any claim can win) or compares the on-chain commitment against data the threat model says checks nothing, which is the exact mistake O1 forbids.
candidates.evidence: Copied the baremetal template, changed 8 RAM bytes, loaded with SHARING_ALL+clear to write a matching cache, destroyed, restored the bytes. cartesi.machine(dir) root = 0xca27de9b... (cache), with clear_hash_tree root = 0x428a6bb8... (contents = commitment). prt.store_first_epoch_checkpoint(dir, {log2_mcycles_per_period=10}, ck0) then load_epoch_checkpoint(ck0) gives manifest.final_state_hash = 0xca27de9b..., which crisium.lua:236 would compare with getTemplateHash() = 0x428a... and abort. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERTEMPLATE/scripts/ckpt.lua.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: build a template with a stale cache as above (contents hash H = root-hash.txt, cached root H' != H); call prt.store_first_epoch_checkpoint; assert load_epoch_checkpoint(dir) manifest.final_state_hash == H (rebuilt). Fails today with H'.

candidates.title: Crafted cached hash-tree files or file modes make adoption fail even with clear_hash_tree (the O1 rebuild cannot run)
candidates.component: Machine loading (memory_address_range, hash_tree, page_hash_tree_cache constructors, os::mapped_memory) and clone_stored, reached by CLI --clear-hash-tree, Lua {clear_hash_tree=true}, and the PRT player
candidates.role: Honest operator (loading/cloning machines); CLI and PRT player are support
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp:303-326 (clear_hash_tree runs only after m_ars and m_ht are constructed from the cache files); src/page-hash-tree-cache.hpp:440-453 and check_metadata :702-727 (throws on tag/metadata); src/hash-tree.cpp:993-1003 (throws 'inconsistent sparse hash tree nodes'); src/os-mapped-memory.cpp:59-69,159-176 (exact length / read-only / link-count checks on .dht/.dpt/.phtc/.bin); src/os-filesystem.cpp:592-617 clone_file (hard-links any file whose mode has no write bit); doc/recipes/prt.lua:3209-3216
candidates.description: clear_hash_tree is applied after the machine has been constructed from the cached hash-tree files, and construction validates those files and throws: a hash_tree.phtc with a wrong tag or LRU metadata, a missing or wrongly sized hash_tree.phtc, a .dht of the wrong length, or sparse nodes with different structure all make cartesi.machine(T,{clear_hash_tree=true}) and cartesi-machine --load=T --clear-hash-tree fail, although these files are exactly the data O1 says to discard and rebuild. Separately, clone_stored decides to hard-link a file from its mode bits, which the supplier controls: a writable range's .bin (or its .dht/.dpt) shipped with mode 0444 is hard-linked into the player's epoch directory, and load with SHARING_ALL then refuses it ('is read-only and cannot be shared for writing'), so the PRT player cannot adopt the template (loading the same directory without sharing works). No documented tool rebuilds or discards the cache files.
candidates.trigger: Template supplier ships a valid template with corrupted/missing cache files or chmod 0444 on a writable range file; operator adopts per O1 with the documented tools.
candidates.reachability: Hashed contents unchanged; only cached hash-tree data and file metadata, which are outside every valid-template condition.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? Not 'Defects that need the cached hash-tree data ... to survive its adoption without a rebuild (O1)': the defect is that the rebuild itself cannot run. Section 5: 'the emulator must make them possible to follow ... A defect that defeats the rebuild itself ... is not excused by them.' Arguably the operator 'may decline' the template.
2 Role: loading/cloning machines = Honest operator; CLI/player = Support.

3 High/Medium: if the template counts as data from other parties that the operator may decline, a loud failure is at most the High case 'crash ... caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline' only if it is a crash; it is an exception, so likely below that. Medium case 'A persistence operation that fails loudly, without a wrong hash ... in an uncommon host setup' does not fit exactly.

4 Critical reading: on the honest operator's path ('Obtaining its valid template ... includes rebuilding its cached hash-tree data (O1)'), O1 cannot be followed with the emulator's tools, so the operator cannot defend a valid template (R4 completeness).
5 Low reading: fails loudly; the operator can delete/recreate the cache files by hand or obtain another copy.
candidates.claimed_severity: High/Critical if O1's 'emulator must make them possible to follow' covers it; otherwise Low
candidates.threat_to_goal: A template supplier (who may also be a dispute adversary) can prevent honest operators that follow O1 from adopting the valid template before the dispute clocks run out.
candidates.evidence: On a copy of the baremetal template, load with {clear_hash_tree=true} (SHARING_NONE and SHARING_ALL): phtc tag overwritten -> error; RAM .dht truncated to 0 -> error; hash_tree.phtc removed or emptied -> error; RAM .dpt removed -> error with SHARING_NONE, OK with SHARING_ALL. chmod 0444 on 0000000080000000-4000000.bin: plain load OK; clone_stored hard-links it (nlink 2) and load(clone,{clear_hash_tree=true},SHARING_ALL) fails 'backing file ... is read-only and cannot be shared for writing when initializing RAM'.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: for each crafted variant (bad phtc tag, missing phtc, truncated dht, 0444 RAM .bin), clone_stored the template and load it with {clear_hash_tree=true} under SHARING_NONE and SHARING_ALL; assert the load succeeds and get_root_hash() equals root-hash.txt.

candidates.title: config.json size and unknown fields are unbounded, parsed in full on every load, and copied verbatim into every player snapshot by clone_stored
candidates.role: Honest operator (loading/cloning machines); PRT player (support) is where the copy multiplies
candidates.location: src/machine-config.cpp:125-151 (reads the whole file and parses it; unknown keys ignored by ju_get_field); src/machine.cpp:566-570 (clone_stored clones config.json byte for byte)
candidates.description: config.json is outside the hashed state. Its size is unbounded and unknown members are silently ignored, so a supplier can pad it (e.g. a 60 MB array of small integers, compressible to almost nothing) and every load of the template or of any clone_stored copy reads and parses all of it with ~5x memory amplification. machine::store normalizes it, but the PRT player builds its epoch machine, revert backups and cache entries with clone_stored, which copies the padded file into each, and loads them repeatedly (every commit/revert/entry). This makes loading cost grow with an unhashed, supplier-chosen quantity rather than with the state.
candidates.trigger: Template supplier pads config.json; operator adopts with the documented tools; PRT player propagates it through clone_stored.
candidates.reachability: Valid template; only unhashed config.json bytes changed.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? Same analysis as candidate 1: the snapshot meets the valid-template conditions; 'nothing it carries outside the hashed state may ... crash the honest operator'.
2 Role: loading/cloning = Honest operator.
3 High: 'unbounded allocation in a component in the honest-operator role, caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline' if the template is declinable data.

4 Critical reading: R12 'storing, loading, cloning or syncing a machine' bounded and at most linear in the bytes it covers, on the honest operator's path; here cost depends on padding outside the state.
5 Low if triage deems a template supplier trusted for its metadata.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Memory/time exhaustion of the honest operator on every load of the template and of every snapshot the player clones from it.
candidates.evidence: Added a 60 MB unknown member to config.json of the baremetal template: load still succeeds with the same root hash; peak RSS 458 MB vs 140 MB, load CPU 1.66 s vs 0.37 s. Unknown members (top level, in config, in ram) are accepted silently.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: pad config.json with an unknown member of N MB; assert load either rejects unknown members / oversized config, or that clone_stored output config.json is normalized (no padding) so snapshots do not inherit it.

not_covered: Did not run the full PRT player/crisium against a chain with a crafted template (only called prt.store_first_epoch_checkpoint / load_epoch_checkpoint directly and the clone+load sequence of new_stored_player).
Did not test very large phtc_size values (2^24+) to observe the actual OOM/SIGBUS (would disturb other agents); extrapolated linearly from 4096 and 65536.
Did not examine the JSON-RPC server's load/store path in detail (prt.new_machine uses it) beyond noting it calls the same machine::load.
Did not audit sparse-file/sparseness effects on os::copy_file (store with SHARING_NONE rollback path) or on non-reflink filesystems (ext4 fallback copy in clone_file).

Did not check symlinked/FIFO/device backing files exhaustively (a FIFO would block open; a symlink to a character device fails length/FICLONE checks) or extra files in the template directory (ignored by clone_stored).

Did not look for wrong-hash effects of cached dht/dpt surviving into the operator's snapshots on paths other than store_first_epoch_checkpoint (all other player and vg.lua adoption paths pass clear_hash_tree).
Did not test phtc_size=1 for performance degradation (hash results were identical).
Did not audit validate_memory_range_label / flash drive label lengths or other free-form config fields that might be consumed by tools.
